title: Jacobi-Zariski exact sequence for H_1 of naive cotangent complexes (Stacks 00S2)
statement:
Let $A\to B\xrightarrow{\ \varphi\ }C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, $C$ an $A$-algebra through the composite. For a ring map $R\to S$ let $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}=\bigl(I_{S/R}/I_{S/R}^2\xrightarrow{\delta_{S/R}}\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\bigr)$ be the naive cotangent complex of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], formed with the canonical presentation $R[S]\to S$, $[s]\mapsto s$, with kernel $I_{S/R}$, and $H_1(L_{S/R})=\ker\delta_{S/R}$; $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC$ be the complex $I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\delta_{B/A}\otimes\mathrm{id}_C}\bigoplus_{b\in B}C\,\mathrm d[b]$ and $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$ its kernel. Define $C$-linear maps:
(a) $u:H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\to H_1(L_{C/A})$, the restriction of $I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}^2\otimes_BC\to I_{C/A}/I_{C/A}^2$, $(g\bmod I_{B/A}^2)\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot(\varphi_\sharp(g)\bmod I_{C/A}^2)$, where $\varphi_\sharp:A[B]\to A[C]$ is the $A$-algebra map $[b]\mapsto[\varphi(b)]$ (the functoriality of $\mathrm{NL}$ for the square $A=A$, $\varphi:B\to C$);
(b) $v:H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})$, the restriction of $I_{C/A}/I_{C/A}^2\to I_{C/B}/I_{C/B}^2$ induced by the ring map $A[C]\to B[C]$ that is $A\to B$ on coefficients and $[c]\mapsto[c]$ (the functoriality of $\mathrm{NL}$ for the square $A\to B$, $C=C$);
(c) $w:C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}$, $c\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto c\,\mathrm d\varphi(b)$, and $z:\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}$, $c\,\mathrm dc'\mapsto c\,\mathrm dc'$.
Then $u$ and $v$ are well defined (they land in the kernels), and there is a $C$-linear map $\partial:H_1(L_{C/B})\to C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$ (the connecting map of the snake lemma; explicitly, if $h=g\bmod I_{C/B}^2\in H_1(L_{C/B})$ with $g=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha[c]^\alpha\in I_{C/B}$ written in the monomials $[c]^\alpha$ of $B[C]$ with coefficients $b_\alpha\in B$, then $\partial(h)=\sum_\alpha\gamma_{C/B}([c]^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm db_\alpha$, where $\gamma_{C/B}:B[C]\to C$ is the canonical presentation) such that the sequence of $C$-modules
$$H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)\xrightarrow{u}H_1(L_{C/A})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow{\partial}C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{C/A}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{C/B}\to0$$
is exact. Moreover, if $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^B_2(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then the natural $C$-linear map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$, $h\otimes c\mapsto h\otimes c$, is an isomorphism.

proof.text: (Presentations.) Let $\alpha:P=A[x_b,\ b\in B]\to B$, $x_b\mapsto b$, be the canonical presentation of $B$ over $A$ ($P=A[B]$, $x_b=[b]$), kernel $I=I_{B/A}$; $\beta:Q=B[y_c,\ c\in C]\to C$, $y_c\mapsto c$, the canonical presentation of $C$ over $B$, kernel $J=I_{C/B}$; $\gamma:P'=A[x_b,y_c]\to C$ the $A$-algebra map with $x_b\mapsto\varphi(b)$, $y_c\mapsto c$ (surjective), kernel $K$; and $\varepsilon:A[z_c,\ c\in C]\to C$, $z_c\mapsto c$, the canonical presentation of $C$ over $A$, kernel $I_{C/A}$. For each presentation $\pi:R[x_t]\to S$ with kernel $I_\pi$, $S\otimes\Omega_{R[x_t]/R}$ is free on the $1\otimes\mathrm dx_t$ and $1\otimes\mathrm dg=\sum_t\pi(\partial g/\partial x_t)(1\otimes\mathrm dx_t)$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables]; so the complex $\mathrm{NL}(\pi)=(I_\pi/I_\pi^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_\pi}S\otimes\Omega_{R[x_t]/R})$ of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] is, under $\mathrm d[s]\leftrightarrow1\otimes\mathrm dx_s$, exactly the complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] when $\pi$ is the canonical presentation. Thus $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)=\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$, $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)=\mathrm{NL}_{C/B}$, $\mathrm{NL}(\varepsilon)=\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}$, and $H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)=\ker(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$.

(Morphisms of presentations.) The inclusion $\iota:P\to P'$, $x_b\mapsto x_b$, satisfies $\gamma\iota=\varphi\alpha$, so it is a morphism of presentations from $\alpha$ to $\gamma$ over the square ($A=A$, $\varphi$); the ring map $\pi:P'\to Q$ that is $A\to B$ on coefficients, $x_b\mapsto b$ (a constant of $Q$) and $y_c\mapsto y_c$, satisfies $\beta\pi=\gamma$, so it is a morphism of presentations from $\gamma$ to $\beta$ over the square ($A\to B$, $\mathrm{id}_C$) [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Hence $\iota(I)\subseteq K$, $\pi(K)\subseteq J$ and we get $C$-linear maps $\iota_1:I/I^2\otimes_BC\to K/K^2$ ($C$-linear extension of the $B$-linear map $\iota_1$ of that node) and $\pi_1:K/K^2\to J/J^2$, and likewise $\iota_0:(B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\otimes_BC\to C\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/A}$ and $\pi_0:C\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/A}\to C\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/B}$, with $\mathrm d_\gamma\iota_1=\iota_0(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$ and $\mathrm d_\beta\pi_1=\pi_0\mathrm d_\gamma$ (same node). Also $\pi\iota(f)=\alpha(f)$ is the constant $\alpha(f)\in B\subseteq Q$, which is $0$ for $f\in I$, so $\pi_1\iota_1=0$; and $\pi_0\iota_0=0$ since $\mathrm d(\pi(x_b))=\mathrm d(b)=0$ in $\Omega_{Q/B}$.

(Top row exact.) By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] the three modules $(B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\otimes_BC$, $C\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/A}$, $C\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/B}$ are free over $C$ on $\{\mathrm dx_b\}$, $\{\mathrm dx_b\}\cup\{\mathrm dy_c\}$, $\{\mathrm dy_c\}$ respectively, and $\iota_0(\mathrm dx_b)=\mathrm dx_b$, $\pi_0(\mathrm dx_b)=\mathrm d(b)=0$, $\pi_0(\mathrm dy_c)=\mathrm dy_c$. Hence $0\to(B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\iota_0}C\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/A}\xrightarrow{\pi_0}C\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/B}\to0$ is exact (it is the split sequence $0\to C^{(B)}\to C^{(B)}\oplus C^{(C)}\to C^{(C)}\to0$).

(Bottom row exact: $I/I^2\otimes_BC\xrightarrow{\iota_1}K/K^2\xrightarrow{\pi_1}J/J^2\to0$.) The map $\pi:P'=P[y_c]\to B[y_c]=Q$ is the coefficientwise map of $\alpha:P\to B$; since $\alpha$ is surjective, $\pi$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak n=I\cdot P'$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel]. As $\gamma=\beta\pi$, $K=\pi^{-1}(J)$, so $\pi(K)=J$ and $\mathfrak n\subseteq K$. Hence $\pi_1$ is surjective, and its kernel is $\{k\bmod K^2: \pi(k)\in J^2\}$; since $\pi^{-1}(J^2)=\pi^{-1}(\pi(K^2))=K^2+\mathfrak n$, this kernel is $(K^2+\mathfrak n)/K^2$, the image of $\mathfrak n=I P'$ in $K/K^2$, i.e. the $P'$-submodule (equivalently $C$-submodule) generated by the classes of $\iota(f)$, $f\in I$, which is the image of $\iota_1$. Together with $\pi_1\iota_1=0$ (step 2) the row is exact.

(Snake lemma.) Steps 2--4 give a commutative diagram of $C$-modules with exact rows $I/I^2\otimes_BC\to K/K^2\to J/J^2\to0$ and $0\to(B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A})\otimes_BC\to C\otimes_{P'}\Omega_{P'/A}\to C\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/B}\to0$ and vertical maps $\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C$, $\mathrm d_\gamma$, $\mathrm d_\beta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] (with $\Lambda=C$) there is a $C$-linear $\partial_0:\ker\mathrm d_\beta\to\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$ with
$$\ker(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\xrightarrow{\iota_1}\ker\mathrm d_\gamma\xrightarrow{\pi_1}\ker\mathrm d_\beta\xrightarrow{\partial_0}\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\xrightarrow{\bar\iota_0}\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\gamma\xrightarrow{\bar\pi_0}\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\beta\to0$$
exact, the final surjectivity because $\pi_0$ is surjective.

(Identifying the cokernels.) By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] applied to $A\to P$ and the ideal $I$ (with $P/I\cong B$ via $\alpha$), $I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_\alpha}B\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}\to\Omega_{B/A}\to0$, $1\otimes\mathrm dg\mapsto\mathrm d\alpha(g)$, is exact, so $\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\alpha\cong\Omega_{B/A}$ with $\mathrm dx_b\mapsto\mathrm db$; tensoring with $C$ keeps this right exact [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], so $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\cong\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\cong C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$, $\mathrm dx_b\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes\mathrm db$. The same node applied to $A\to P'$, $K$ and to $B\to Q$, $J$ gives $\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\gamma\cong\Omega_{C/A}$ ($\mathrm dx_b\mapsto\mathrm d\varphi(b)$, $\mathrm dy_c\mapsto\mathrm dc$) and $\operatorname{coker}\mathrm d_\beta\cong\Omega_{C/B}$ ($\mathrm dy_c\mapsto\mathrm dc$). Under these isomorphisms $\bar\iota_0$ becomes $c\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto c\,\mathrm d\varphi(b)$, i.e. $w$, and $\bar\pi_0$ sends $\mathrm d\varphi(b)$ (the image of $\mathrm dx_b$) to $0=z(\mathrm d\varphi(b))$ and $\mathrm dc$ (image of $\mathrm dy_c$) to $\mathrm dc=z(\mathrm dc)$; as the $\mathrm d\varphi(b)$, $\mathrm dc$ generate $\Omega_{C/A}$, $\bar\pi_0$ becomes $z$. Define $\partial$ as $\partial_0$ followed by the isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\cong C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$; by step 1, $\ker\mathrm d_\beta=H_1(L_{C/B})$. Step 5 then gives exactness of $H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow{\partial}C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{C/A}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{C/B}\to0$ and $\operatorname{im}(\pi_1|_{\ker\mathrm d_\gamma})=\ker\partial$.

(Identifying $\ker\mathrm d_\gamma$ with $H_1(L_{C/A})$ and the maps $u$, $v$.) Let $\psi:A[z_c]\to P'$, $z_c\mapsto y_c$, and $\theta:P'\to A[z_c]$, $x_b\mapsto z_{\varphi(b)}$, $y_c\mapsto z_c$ ($A$-algebra maps). Then $\gamma\psi=\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon\theta=\gamma$, so $\psi$ is a morphism of presentations from $\varepsilon$ to $\gamma$ and $\theta$ one from $\gamma$ to $\varepsilon$, over identity squares. Since $\theta\psi=\mathrm{id}$, $\theta_*\psi_*=\mathrm{id}$; since $\psi\theta$ and $\mathrm{id}_{P'}$ are both morphisms of presentations from $\gamma$ to $\gamma$, $\psi_*\theta_*=(\psi\theta)_*=(\mathrm{id}_{P'})_*=\mathrm{id}$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (1), (2). So $\psi_*:H_1(L_{C/A})=\ker\mathrm d_\varepsilon\to\ker\mathrm d_\gamma$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\theta_*$. Moreover $\theta\iota:A[x_b]\to A[z_c]$ is $x_b\mapsto z_{\varphi(b)}$, i.e. $\varphi_\sharp$, so $\theta_*\circ\iota_1=u$ on $\ker(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$ (both are $(g\bmod I^2)\otimes c\mapsto c\,(\varphi_\sharp(g)\bmod I_{C/A}^2)$; in particular $u$ is well defined and lands in $H_1(L_{C/A})$); and $\pi\psi:A[z_c]\to Q=B[y_c]$ is $A\to B$ on coefficients and $z_c\mapsto y_c$, i.e. the map defining $v$, so $\pi_1\circ\psi_*=v$ (and $v$ lands in $H_1(L_{C/B})$) by composition (2) of that node.

(Exactness at $H_1(L_{C/A})$ and at $H_1(L_{C/B})$.) From step 5, $\operatorname{im}\iota_1=\ker(\pi_1|_{\ker\mathrm d_\gamma})$ in $\ker\mathrm d_\gamma$. Applying the isomorphism $\theta_*=\psi_*^{-1}$ of step 7: $\operatorname{im}u=\theta_*(\operatorname{im}\iota_1)=\theta_*(\ker\pi_1)=\ker(\pi_1\psi_*)=\ker v$. And $\ker\partial=\operatorname{im}\pi_1=\operatorname{im}(\pi_1\psi_*)=\operatorname{im}v$ since $\psi_*$ is surjective onto $\ker\mathrm d_\gamma$ (step 6 for the first equality). With step 6 the whole six-term sequence is exact.

(Tor clause.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-two-term-complex-kernel-base-change] to the $B$-linear map $\delta_{B/A}:N_1=I/I^2\to N_0=\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b]$, whose target is free, with kernel $H_1(L_{B/A})$ and cokernel $\Omega_{B/A}$ (step 6, via step 1). If $\operatorname{Tor}^B_1(\Omega_{B/A},C)=\operatorname{Tor}^B_2(\Omega_{B/A},C)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], the map $H_1(L_{B/A})\otimes_BC\to\ker(\delta_{B/A}\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)=H_1(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_BC)$, $h\otimes c\mapsto h\otimes c$, is an isomorphism; it is $C$-linear.

(Explicit form of $\partial$.) Let $h=g\bmod J^2\in\ker\mathrm d_\beta$ with $g=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha y^\alpha\in J$ ($b_\alpha\in B$, $y^\alpha$ the monomials in the $y_c$, coefficients unique). Put $g'=\sum_\alpha x_{b_\alpha}y^\alpha\in P'$. Then $\pi(g')=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha y^\alpha=g$, so $g'\in\pi^{-1}(J)=K$ (step 4) and $\pi_1(g'\bmod K^2)=h$: $g'\bmod K^2$ is a lift of $h$ as required in the construction of the connecting map in [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] (step 1), $\mathrm d_\gamma(g'\bmod K^2)=\sum_b\gamma(\partial g'/\partial x_b)\,\mathrm dx_b+\sum_c\gamma(\partial g'/\partial y_c)\,\mathrm dy_c$. Here $\partial g'/\partial x_b=\sum_{\alpha:\,b_\alpha=b}y^\alpha$, so the first sum is $\sum_\alpha\gamma(y^\alpha)\,\mathrm dx_{b_\alpha}=\iota_0\big(\sum_\alpha\mathrm dx_{b_\alpha}\otimes\beta(y^\alpha)\big)$ (as $\gamma(y^\alpha)=\beta(y^\alpha)$); and $\gamma(\partial g'/\partial y_c)=\sum_\alpha\varphi(b_\alpha)\,\beta(\partial y^\alpha/\partial y_c)=\beta(\partial g/\partial y_c)$, which is $0$ for every $c$ because $\mathrm d_\beta(h)=\sum_c\beta(\partial g/\partial y_c)\,\mathrm dy_c=0$ and the $\mathrm dy_c$ are a basis (step 3). So $\mathrm d_\gamma(g'\bmod K^2)=\iota_0(u)$ with $u=\sum_\alpha\mathrm dx_{b_\alpha}\otimes\beta(y^\alpha)$, and by the construction in [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules], $\partial_0(h)=u\bmod\operatorname{im}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)$. Under the isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}(\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)\cong C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$, $\mathrm dx_b\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes\mathrm db$, of step 6, this gives $\partial(h)=\sum_\alpha\beta(y^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm db_\alpha$, which is the explicit formula of the statement ($y^\alpha=[c]^\alpha$, $\beta=\gamma_{C/B}$).
